Migration finished. 12 files were still on `db.query`, 3 call sites each (36 total), all converted to `db.execute({ sql, params })` matching the pattern used in the already-migrated files:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `src/repo/session.js`, `src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `src/service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `src/repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `src/repo/refund.js`, `src/service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `src/repo/supplier.js`, `src/admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `src/repo/shipment.js`, `src/service/returnService.js` |
| support | `src/repo/sla.js`, `src/admin/macroAdmin.js` |

All 12 pass `node --check`. No non-JS references to `db.query` exist (no docs/tests in the repo).

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — still calls `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade, with local edits silently lost. Patching it there wouldn't survive. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix: either upgrade legacy-orm to a version on the new API, or wrap the adapter at the call boundary. Worth tracking separately — I didn't want to make an edit that looks done but gets reverted on the next vendor bump.
- **`cache.query(...)`** in the repo files — that's the cache handle, unrelated to the db migration.

`lib/db.js` still exports the deprecated `query` method; it can be removed once the vendor adapter is resolved.
